title: Distance to bank as IV for savings rate

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use an instrumental variable (IV) approach to estimate the causal effect of having a bank account on household savings. The key assumption is that the instrument (distance to the nearest bank branch) is correlated with the endogenous variable (having a bank account) and affects the outcome (household savings) only through the endogenous variable.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(lmtest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s20_data.csv")

# First stage: distance to account ownership
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)

# Second stage: savings on predicted account ownership
second_stage <- feols(y ~ x + controls | 0 | z, data = data)

# Print the coefficient of the predicted account ownership in the second stage
print(coef(second_stage)["x"])

# Robustness check: test for weak instruments
library(plm)
ivreg_fe <- ivreg(y ~ x | 0 | z, data = data)
library(lmtest)
waldtest(ivreg_fe, "x", order.by = "z")

# Robustness check: test for overidentifying restrictions
overid_test <- ovtest(ivreg_fe)
print(overid_test)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient of the predicted account ownership in the second stage to be positive, indicating that having a bank account increases household savings. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the strength of the instrument and the relationship between account ownership and savings. If the instrument is strong and the relationship is causal, we expect a substantial positive effect. However, if the instrument is weak or the relationship is not causal, the effect may be smaller or even non-significant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: branch distance; first stage: distance → account ownership (negative)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Bank account ownership significantly increases savings
_ground_truth.main_effect: Having an account increases monthly savings by ~40% (IV estimate)
